final_text:
I've checked R1 to R8 against the eleven files. Only two of the eight are ready to send as they stand. I copied every quote into the pack word for word, then searched for each of the 32 quotes in its source file again, and all were found.

The pack is in `evidence_tannwald_R1-R8.md`. It has the file index, a test table for each request, the counts, and draft questions to the people who can close each gap. I used the audit date of 10 December 2026 and the request's own cut-off: documents must be dated on or after 10 December 2025.

| # | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| R1 Systems and storage country | **Ready** | System list approved 2 Sept 2026. It shows three systems in Germany and Claude Team in the United States. |
| R2 Sub-processors | **Missing** | The Anthropic row has no review date and no legal basis for the US transfer. Its contract date is only "accepted online 2026-09-01". The other three vendors are complete. |
| R3 AI tools | **Missing** | The AI rule only applies from 1 Oct, but Claude has been in use since 1 Sept, so September had no rule. The IT lead's personal notes also mention a free chatbot that agents used on their phones until September. Nothing records which tool it was or what data went into it. |
| R4 Admin account review | **Missing** | Only Servicepult was reviewed (14 Aug 2026). Sprechband, Nordlager and Claude Team have no review. |
| R5 Training | **Missing** | 25 of 120 staff are trained (20.8%), against the 95% required (114 staff). There is no data protection course at all, only the Claude intro. One person appears twice; I removed the repeat before counting. |
| R6 Incidents | **Ready** | One incident with Tannwald data (INC-02). Tannwald was told 30.5 hours after detection, within the 48 hours required. |
| R7 Restore test | **Missing** | The backup report says "Restore test: not done in 2026." |
| R8 Security policy | **Out of date** | The approved version 3 dates from 12 March 2024 and was due for review in March 2025. Version 4 is still a draft with no approval. |

**Result: 2 ready, 1 out of date, 5 missing.**

These issues aren't separate requests, but management needs to decide on them before anything goes to Tannwald:
- **Clause 7 (data location):** Claude stores data in the US, and the folder has no written agreement from Tannwald to that. The only claim that "data stays in Europe" was a verbal remark from a vendor rep. The vendor page says the data is stored in the US.
- **Clause 7 (written notice):** I found no written notice to Tannwald that Claude is used. The IT lead's own note says "I found nothing."
- **The free chatbot use:** it isn't in the incident log. If management counts it as an incident involving Tannwald data, R6 is no longer ready either.
- **The current policy's own rules:** version 3 requires an admin-access review every quarter and a restore test twice a year. The folder has one admin review, covering one system, and no restore test.

The pack includes draft questions for the IT lead, the HR lead and the Managing Director. I've asked for replies by 20 November so there is time before the 25 November deadline. Each one says that "does not exist" is a fine answer. The Claude storage location rests on a vendor page dated 15 June 2026, so read the live page again before sending.

The statuses show what the folder contains today. What actually goes to Tannwald, and who signs it, is your decision.
